HIGH — the planned carry-forward departs from the adopted contract's Repair rule and mutant stop condition, and neither the amendment nor the inventory says so. Requirement (adopted-contract.json boundaryPacket.expectedEffects[28], unchanged in 56d428bb): after a B5 repair `bind-candidate-tree runs; prepare-bdd reruns in the main tree; the old M1/M2 worktrees are removed ... and recreated, digest-checked, patched and rebuilt from the new commit; the baseline checks rerun when the diff touches tests/bdd/**`. evidenceInvalidation: `Both mutant controls always rerun after a repair, because their worktrees are recreated from the new candidate.` stopConditions[10]: a mutant whose `diff lists any file other than the inventory target` makes the control INVALID and SCN-SYS-015 / SCN-SYS-017 BLOCKED. Observed: both mutant worktrees are detached at 2723a97b; `git -C ~/.claude/worktrees/s1-mutant-m1 diff --name-only c8eb9e23` lists src/uar/runtime/manager.rs, static/.vite/markdown-engine-graph.json, static/index.html and tests/bdd/playwright.config.ts (M2: same with src/uar/domain/policy.rs). verify-mutant-m1-diff and verify-mutant-m2-diff (commands 13, 20) passed with C=2723a97b; run today against the inventory candidateCommit they fail. prepare-bdd last ran 10:46-11:19 on ae01b21c (boundary/logs/01-prepare-bdd.log, static/ mtime 10:46), two commits and two binds ago. The 56d428bb amendment changed only the two cp insertions; its own `unchanged` list names `verdict rules ... mutant patches and builds, and command order`, so it is not a waiver of the Repair rule. Its reason text does admit the worktrees come `from the previous candidate`, which leaves the contract saying both things. inventory.unverified reports the builds as `Carried forward without rerun` with no mention of the rule or of an operator exception, and names only command 7 for rerun although the rule says `the baseline checks`. Consequence: SCN-SYS-015, SCN-SYS-017 and every BDD scenario could be recorded PASS under a contract whose own terms mark the mutant controls INVALID and require the rebuild; the result is contestable the first time anyone reads the rule. Technical equivalence does hold on what I could check (see mutants and dryWalk): the two commits differ only in the harness file, and each mutant tree after the cp equals candidate + its target file + build outputs. Fix, one of: (a) follow the rule: rerun 0 and 1, `scripts/worktree-rm.sh s1-mutant-m1 --force` and `s1-mutant-m2 --force`, rerun 9-22, rerun 7 and 8, then 23-49; or (b) an operator-signed amendment that states the round-2 exception in the rule text itself (mutant worktrees and builds from 2723a97b kept on the byte-equivalence basis, what replaces the 13/20 diff check, whether prepare-bdd and command 8 rerun), then regenerate inventory.unverified to name the exception. Rerunning command 1 is cheap either way and should not be waived (next note).

LOW — service workers are not blocked in the BDD config. frontend/src/main.tsx:46-50 registers /sw.js on load; static/sw.js (identical to frontend/public/sw.js) calls skipWaiting and clients.claim, so it takes control of the page mid-test. Playwright's own type docs (node_modules/.pnpm/playwright-core@1.64.1/.../types/types.d.ts:10402) say page.route `will not intercept requests intercepted by Service Worker` and recommend serviceWorkers 'block'; six frontend Playwright configs in this repo set it. The one S1 interception, tests/bdd/steps/live-model-choice.steps.ts:309 (`**/api/uar/providers/*/default`, a POST), targets a request the worker leaves alone: static/sw.js:40-47 returns without respondWith for any non-GET and for /api/, /v1/, /metrics. The write log (tests/bdd/support/s1.ts:104-116) records only non-GET /api/uar/ requests, the same class. By reading, interception and the write log are unaffected; I did not confirm by execution how Chromium reports a fetch the worker declines. The dev server served the same /sw.js, so this is not new with c8eb9e23, but no S1 scenario ever got far enough on either harness to exercise it. Fix if it bites: `serviceWorkers: 'block'` in use{} (new candidate).
